title: What Are the Samoan Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget

refresh_of.note: Person: article to refresh. Publish method: update in place, change slug and path to /expert-advice/samoan-wedding-traditions, confirm the old URL returns a 301. Check for duplicate Samoan or Pacific wedding pages. Protect its rankings.

notes: REFRESH: the brief reads the old page with mcp__Apify__apify--web-fetch (one render-wait retry if the body is empty; if the call is DECLINED, do not retry and infer coverage from rankings). SEO pulls its ranked keywords (US and AU), checks duplicates, and the outline keeps covering every query with real volume. Drop the 'shocked and excited' framing. Never reuse wording; drop errors.

AUTHORITY RULE (content-system/brand/voice-guide.md 'Write with authority'): no research talk in the copy (what we could or couldn't find, trace or confirm; our sources or method; what the internet says; myths sections; 'you will often read'). Customs without a strong source are written as living practice in a confident voice ('In many Samoan families...'), never with a meaning or origin stated as fact. 'Often told' at most once per post, never 'it is often told that'. No hedge stacking: cite a source once by link; date legal and travel facts once per section. Source gaps go in the run report only.
Fa'a Samoa: families, matai and the church are central; respectful framing. Samoan terms and diacritics as sources give them. Diaspora in Australia and New Zealand.

Likely customs (brief finalises): the families' formal meeting and tulafale (orator) speeches; exchange of fine mats ('ie toga) and gifts between families with no amounts; the church wedding; dress (puletasi, ie faitaga); siva and the taualuga; the feast; extended family and village roles.
UNESCO only where its own text links an element to weddings (for example the 'ie Samoa fine mat listing, if confirmed live).

Destination angle: Smartraveller Samoa checked live. Legal from official sources only: Australian High Commission Apia (CNI, notarial), Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (recognition), Samoa's Births, Deaths and Marriages registry (Ministry of Justice and Courts Administration) only if an official page can be read; otherwise 'check with the registry and the high commission, including any fees'; 'as at November 2026'. Upolu and Savai'i named only as places couples choose; no venue claims.

Sources: Samoa government, samoa.travel, Ministry of Education, Sports and Culture, Te Papa, Auckland Museum, Australian Museum, UNESCO, encyclopaedias, academic sources. Never competitor wedding sites, vendor blogs or Wikipedia.

Links: Oceania hub and Fiji pages from the link map as Pacific destinations; never the Fiji magazine (do-not-link). UTMs: utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=samoan-wedding-traditions&utm_content=primary|secondary.

Images: placeholders only; no AI images of people, cultural dress, ceremonies or places; AI only for neutral still lifes (woven mat, frangipani) labelled illustrative pending approval; old-page images only if licence confirmed.

Speed: WebFetch cannot reach outside sites; Apify web-fetch (parallel) and DataForSEO from the start. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches (A: families' meeting, speeches, fine mats and gifts, church wedding; B: dress, dance, feast, UNESCO and legal), 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, separate scratch folders; self_qa.confidence must be a number; must_include_coverage entries must be objects with covered_by as an array; no extra sourcing rounds; never retry a declined call.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.

Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance' or 'last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions in writing); no implied help with legal or church paperwork.
Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts; no vendor or venue names; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
